For an integer \(t\ge 2\), consider all integers \(k\ge t\), finite sets \(V\), and families \(\mathcal F\) of \(k\)-element subsets of \(V\) with the following properties. The family is intersecting, meaning that \(F\cap F'\ne\varnothing\) for all \(F,F'\in\mathcal F\). Its covering number is \(t\), where the covering number is the minimum cardinality of a set \(C\subseteq V\) meeting every member of \(\mathcal F\).

In addition, choose a partition \(\mathcal F=\mathcal F_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup\mathcal F_t\) into nonempty subfamilies and pairwise disjoint nonempty sets \(X_1,\ldots,X_t\subseteq V\) such that \(X_i\subseteq F\) for every \(F\in\mathcal F_i\). Define
\[
b(t)=\min\sum_{i=1}^{t}\bigl(k-|X_i|\bigr),
\]
where the minimum ranges over all the choices just described, including \(k\) and \(V\).

With \(\log\) denoting the natural logarithm, determine the exact value of
\[
\lim_{\substack{t\to\infty\\t\in\mathbb Z}}\frac{\log b(t)}{\log t}.
\]

### General bad-coalition argument to finish

Setup clean star construction below. Petal families \(\mathcal P_i\) on actual points \(E(K_n)\), \(G\) \(h\)-regular, owner colors \(i=ab\in E(G)\). Remove all petals containing actual point \(v=xy\). For an actual selected point set \(S\) not containing \(v\), let \(J(S)\) be owner colors whose entire surviving petal family is hit by \(S\).

For owner edge \(ab\), surviving center-\(a\) petals:
- originally all \(r\)-subsets of \(U_a=\mathrm{St}(a)\setminus\{ab\}\), \(|U_a|=n-2\).
- if \(v\in U_a\), surviving petals are \(r\)-subsets of \(U_a\setminus\{v\}\), so hitting threshold drops from \(h\) to \(h-1\).
- if \(v=ab\) or \(a\notin v\), threshold stays \(h\).

Thus exact activation:
\[
d_S(a)-1_{\{ab\in S\}}\ge h-1_{\{a\in v,\ ab\ne v\}},
\]
and analogous at \(b\).

Old Hall implies after avoidance \(|J(S)|\le |S|+1\). A bad coalition exists iff some \(S\) has \(|J(S)|=|S|+1\), and minimal bad coalitions are minimal such activated sets \(J(S)\). Any extra private color points just pay 1 for a color, so this reduction is exact.

Let \(W\) be endpoints of activated owner edges \(J(S)\). Then:
- \(|J(S)|\le e_G(W)\le h|W|/2\).
- Each \(a\in W\) has \(d_S(a)\ge h-1_{\{a\in v\}}\) (plus possible own-edge corrections).
- So \(2|S|\ge \sum_{a\in W}d_S(a)\ge h|W|-2\).
- If \(|J(S)|=|S|+1\), inequalities all equalities.
Consequences:
  1. Both endpoints \(x,y\) of \(v\) are in \(W\).
  2. \(J(S)=E_G(W)\), and every vertex of \(W\) has all its \(G\)-neighbors in \(W\), so \(W\) is union of whole connected components of \(G\).
  3. All \(S\)-edges lie inside \(W\), degrees \(h\) except \(x,y\) degree \(h-1\).
  4. No owner edge of \(G\) can belong to \(S\) if it is activated, since own-edge threshold would increase and break equality.
  5. If \(v\in E(G)\), the threshold does NOT drop for owner \(v\), while \(J=E_G(W)\) includes \(v\); equality forces degrees \(h-1\) at both ends, contradiction. Hence no bad coalition for owner actual points.
  6. If \(v\notin G\), every bad coalition contains **all owner edges of the component containing \(x\)** (also component containing \(y\)). Therefore any single owner color in \(x\)'s component hits every bad coalition. Thus \(\lambda_v\le1\), regardless existence.
No need to prove existence for general \(h\) to conclude \(\lambda\le1\). This argument is probably ready.

For \(h\ge2\):
- \(n=2h^2\).
- Let \(G\) be disjoint union of \(h\) copies of \(K_{h,h}\), so \(G\) is \(h\)-regular on \(n\) vertices.
- Owner classes indexed by \(E(G)\), so \(T=h^3\).
- Actual point set \(W=E(K_n)\), outside all eventual cores.

- For owner color \(i=ab\in G\), \(\mathcal P_i\) contains all \(r\)-subsets of \(\mathrm{St}(a)\setminus\{ab\}\), and all \(r\)-subsets of \(\mathrm{St}(b)\setminus\{ab\}\).
- Each petal has a unique center for \(r\ge2\).

For a petal \(P\) centered at \(a\):
\[
O(P)=\{c\ne a:ac\notin P\},\quad |O(P)|=h.
\]
Let \(S(P)\) be all owner edges of \(G\) incident with at least one vertex of \(O(P)\), except its own owner \(i\). Since other endpoint \(b\in O(P)\), own owner was counted, hence
\[
|S(P)|\le h^2-1.
\]
Extend \(S(P)\) arbitrarily to a target set \(L(P)\) of **exactly** \(\ell=h^2-1\) colors excluding \(i\); possible since \(T-1\ge\ell\).

Take disjoint cores \(X_i\), each of cardinality \(T\), outside \(W\). For every \(P\in\mathcal P_i\), include all sets
\[
X_i\cup P\cup\{x_j:j\in L(P)\},
\]
independent arbitrary \(x_j\in X_j\).

Uniform rank:
\[
k=T+r+\ell,\qquad d_i=k-|X_i|=D=r+\ell=3h^2-h-2.
\]
No private padding needed. Distinct classes disjoint as families because a member contains full own \(X_i\), but at most one point of any other core.

Intersection:
- same class share core.
- if actual petals intersect, done.
- same center petals always intersect because \(2r>n-1\).
- different centers \(a,c\), their only possible common actual point is \(ac\). If disjoint, at least one omits \(ac\). Say \(P\) omits it, then \(c\in O(P)\), so the other owner color (incident to \(c\)) is in \(L(P)\). Thus first member hits entire core of second.

Key Hall degree charge:
For actual point set \(A\subseteq W\), let \(J(A)\) be colors whose whole \(\mathcal P_i\) is hit. For owner \(ab\), this means
\[
d_A(a)-1_{\{ab\in A\}}\ge h,\quad d_A(b)-1_{\{ab\in A\}}\ge h.
\]
In particular both endpoints in \(Z=\{a:d_A(a)\ge h\}\). Therefore
\[
|J(A)|\le e_G(Z)\le h|Z|/2\le |A|.
\]
This exact formula and inequality have been exhaustively verified on small examples.

Covering number \(T\):
- one core representative/class gives cover \(T\).
- If \(|C|<T\), no core exhausted. Let \(A=C\cap W\), \(B=\{i:C\cap X_i\ne\varnothing\}\).
- For any \(i\notin B\), if some petal \(P\) misses \(A\), choose all its target-core points outside \(C\), producing a member disjoint from \(C\).
- Thus \(T-|B|\le|J(A)|\le|A|\), yielding \(|C|\ge |A|+|B|\ge T\), contradiction.

All integer \(t\):
Any subunion of \(t\) classes of a \(T\)-class valid instance has covering number exactly \(t\). Otherwise add one core representative per omitted class, contradict total \(\tau=T\).
Choose \(h=\lceil t^{1/3}\rceil\), retain any \(t\) classes. Hence
\[
b(t)\le t(3h^2-h-2)=(3+o(1))t^{5/3}.
\]
In particular limsup \(\le5/3\). This disproves all our earlier quadratic guesses/lemmas.

## Structural facts, reliable

1. For every class subset \(I\),
\[
\tau(\cup_{i\in I}\mathcal F_i)=|I|.
\]
Lower because supplement any smaller cover with core reps outside I. Upper trivial.
Also for petal families \(\mathcal P_i\),
\[
\tau(\cup_{i\in I}\mathcal P_i)\ge|I|.
\]
Equivalent conservative covering: any point set C wholly covers at most |C| color families.
2. Full intersections \(\cap\mathcal F_i\) are pairwise disjoint (otherwise cover 2 classes with one point).
3. Can pad every core by arbitrarily many private points, increasing k uniformly, di unchanged, tau unchanged. Thus k itself not informative.
4. For disjoint I,J, any minimum covers \(C_I,C_J\) are disjoint. More generally
\[
|C_I\cap C_J|\le |I\cap J|.
\]
Thus for each point v, coalitions I whose minimum covers may use v form an intersecting family.
5. Let \(Y_i\subset X_i\) be core points occurring in petals of other classes. Any \(F\in\mathcal F_i\) gives cover \(Y_i\cup(F\setminus X_i)\cup\{x_i\}\), so
\[
|Y_i|\ge t-d_i-1,\quad \sum |Y_i|\ge t(t-1)-D.
\]
This leads possible 5/3 lower route: if after critical pruning/normalization could bound total essential used core points \(O(d^3)\), then \(t=O(d^{3/2})\).
6. Deleting class i and all members of other classes containing a chosen \(p\in X_i\) leaves \(t-1\) nonempty classes, intersecting, tau=t−1.

Let m,n be positive integers with n>4m-1. Put T=nm and r=n-2m.
Let the actual points be the edges of K_n. There are m colors/classes for
each center a in [n]. Give every class i its own disjoint T-point core X_i,
outside all actual points.

For every r-subset P of the (n-1)-edge star at a, let O(P) be the 2m-1
other centers b such that ab is omitted from P. Let L(P) be all m classes
at every center in O(P), so |L(P)|=ell=m(2m-1).
For each class i centered at a, include every set
 X_i union P union {x_j:j in L(P)},
where all choices x_j in X_j are independent. The rank is
 k=T+r+ell=T+n+2m^2-3m,
and every deficit equals D=n+2m^2-3m.

Distinct classes give distinct sets, as one set contains its complete own
T-point core and at most one point of each other core. Every class is
nonempty. All cores are disjoint and nonempty.

Intersection: same-class members share their core. Same-center petals
intersect since 2r>n-1. For different centers a,b, disjoint petals force
at least one to omit actual point ab. If P at a omits ab, it includes
one representative of every class at b, hence intersects the full core
of the other member.

Covering number: selecting one representative of each core gives a
T-point cover. Conversely suppose |C|<T. No core is exhausted. Let
A be C's actual edges, and B the classes whose cores C meets. For each
class outside B, its whole petal family must be met by A, because any
petal disjoint from A can have all its independent target-core choices
made outside C. A hits every r-subset of center a's (n-1)-edge star iff
d_A(a)>=n-r=2m. Thus, writing Z={a:d_A(a)>=2m},

But |C|>=|A|+|B|, a contradiction.

Taking n=m^2, m>=4, gives T=m^3, D=3m^2-3m. For arbitrary large t take
m=ceil(t^(1/3)) and keep any t classes. Every subunion of t classes has
covering number t: a cover of size<t could be supplemented with one
core representative per omitted class to cover the whole original
family in fewer than T points. Therefore
 b(t)<=t(3 ceil(t^(1/3))^2-3 ceil(t^(1/3)))=(3+o(1))t^(5/3).

The asymptotic leading constant from this construction can be optimized:
take n=4m^2, giving T=4m^3, D=6m^2-3m and constant 6/4^(2/3).

actual set S not containing v, let J(S) be colors whose entire remaining
petal family is met by S. Exactly,

 deg_S(a)-1_{ab in S} >= h-1_{a in {x,y}, ab != v},
 deg_S(b)-1_{ab in S} >= h-1_{b in {x,y}, ab != v}.
(The formulas follow from the transversal number of all r-subsets of a
q-point set being q-r+1.) In particular old Hall plus one removed point
gives |J(S)|<=|S|+1.

A color coalition I becomes bad precisely when some actual S has
|I intersect J(S)|>|S|, since all other colors in I can be covered by
one private core label each. Consequently every minimal bad coalition
is J(S) with |J(S)|=|S|+1.

For such S let W be endpoints of J(S). Every a in W has
 deg_S(a)>=h-1_{a in {x,y}}.
Thus

The assumed equality |J(S)|=|S|+1 forces equality throughout. It follows
that x,y are in W; J(S)=E_G(W); every G-neighbor of any W-vertex is in W

both endpoints in W; and degrees in S are h except at x,y, where they
are h-1. No edge of G can belong to S, since any activated own edge in S
would raise a required endpoint degree above these forced values.

activated owner. But this owner's threshold remains h at x and y,
contradicting their forced S-degrees h-1. Thus there are NO bad coalitions.

owner edge of x's component (and y's component). Therefore any single

cores X_i, call x in X_i used if it belongs to a member of a class other
than i. Let N be the total number of used core points.

covering number t-1 exactly when some old minimum t-cover contains both
v and w, and new covering number t otherwise. In the latter case it is
a valid configuration with exactly the same deficits. If v,w are used,
its number of used core points is at most N-1.

replacing z, if present, by v,w. Moreover tau(Q)=t-1 iff an old minimum
t-cover contains both v,w. The forward direction follows by lifting a
(t-1)-cover; it must use z and its lift is a t-cover. The reverse
direction follows by applying q to such an old t-cover.

The quotient members of class i have size k-1, as they contain both v,w;
other members have size k unless they originally contained both v,w.
Adjoin a fresh private point u to every quotient member of class i.
The new core is X_i'=(X_i minus {v,w}) union {z,u}; other cores are fixed.

any cover using u can replace it by z without increasing its cardinality,
and every cover of Q remains a cover after the addition.

by all k-sets E union {a}, a in R, where R is a fresh reservoir of t+1
points outside all cores. (The same R may serve all short members.)

at most t misses some a in R; for each short E the member E union {a}

t or t-1 according to the exact criterion above.

classes may now have duplicate members: assign each distinct member to
any one source class that produced it. It still contains that source's

representative of each remaining core would cover H in at most t-1

does not increase N, and strictly lowers M if N is unchanged. These are
nonnegative integers, and at each operation rank k and t are fixed, so

maximum deficit d, which would give the desired 5/3 lower bound using

Now repeatedly perform either of these operations:

 (b) delete a residual point p from a member F whenever doing so preserves
     intersection with every other member.
